AnalysisTelemetry.description:
Auditable model-call record (Day-2 acceptance: call records are checkable).

``request_id`` stays ``None`` until a real Bedrock call happens, so a local
run can never be mistaken for a cloud one. Counts/durations/identifiers only.
AnalysisTelemetry.title: AnalysisTelemetry

DemoAck.description: Echoes what changed so the UI never has to guess the new facts_version.
DemoAck.title: DemoAck

DemoDeviceModeIn.description: Injects the SIMULATED actuator outcome for NEW commands only.
DemoDeviceModeIn.title: DemoDeviceModeIn

DemoFactsIn.description:
Demo-only fact injection (Day-2 ruling 13).

``extra='forbid'`` IS the hard-quota guard: the limits themselves
(``daily_limit_grams`` / ``single_serving_grams`` / ``minimum_interval_minutes``)
can never be edited through this endpoint, so a demo request cannot raise the
daily budget. ``clear`` distinguishes "leave unchanged" from "set to unknown";
naming a field in both places is a conflict and is rejected.
DemoFactsIn.title: DemoFactsIn

ErrorResponse.description: Shared error body, declared in OpenAPI ``responses`` (401/403/404/409).
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

EvidenceItem.description:
One read-only tool call that really happened.

Tool name, source, timestamp and a bounded summary only: never hidden
reasoning, never the raw event note, never the full model request.
EvidenceItem.title: EvidenceItem

FeedbackView.description:
Owner feedback plus its HONEST long-term-memory lifecycle.

``memory_status='saved'`` means the raw text is stored in the business
database; it never implies extraction. ``memory_backend`` is carried alongside
so a judge can never read ``saved`` as "AgentCore memory available"
(AGENTS.md L18). ``available`` only ever appears with real retrieval evidence.
FeedbackView.title: FeedbackView

NewSessionView.description:
Result of ``POST /api/demo/new-session``: a fresh conversation id.

Pet memory, facts and the login session are preserved; only the conversation
(the AgentCore session id) rotates, which is what makes cross-session
retrieval demonstrable. The conversation id is never a pet identity.
NewSessionView.title: NewSessionView

post.description:
Inject the SIMULATED actuator outcome for NEW commands only.

Process-local by design: it is not persisted, so a restart returns to the
documented default instead of surprising the next demo with a stale failure.
Inject demo facts. Only the two injectable fields; never the hard limits.

Rotate the conversation id; login, facts and pet memory stay intact.

The conversation id is the AgentCore session id, never a pet identity: memory
retrieval is namespaced by owner/pet, so a fresh conversation still reaches the
same long-term memory (that is what makes cross-session retrieval honest).

post.description:
Store raw owner feedback, then ask the memory backend to process it.

The raw text is persisted FIRST (T5) so a retry carrying the same
``Idempotency-Key`` header reuses the stored feedback id and never submits
twice. The honest lifecycle is decided by the memory backend: locally it stays
``saved`` (nothing is extracted), so it is never reported as ``available``.
